scenes.tts: Turn a newt's eye upside down, then cut the optic nerve and let it regrow. Hold a lure above its head, and the newt turns its head down. It kept making that mistake for as long as anyone watched. Sperry inferred that each regrown axon went back to the place it came from. How does an axon know where to go?

scenes.tts: The retina sends its axons to a target in the midbrain, the tectum. The map is orderly. Neighbors in the retina connect to neighbors in the tectum. In the chick, axons from the temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, end in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons end in the back.
scenes.visual: Retina bar to tectum bar, ordered lines, neighbours highlighted, temporal to front and nasal to back
scenes.narration: The retina sends its axons to a target in the midbrain, the tectum. The map is orderly. Neighbors in the retina connect to neighbors in the tectum. In the chick, axons from the temporal retina, the side nearer the temple, end in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons end in the back.

scenes.tts: A growth cone is the moving tip of an axon. It senses only what is close, yet the map spans the whole target. The answer is a pair of opposite slopes. In the retina, the receptor Eff A is high on the temporal side and low on the nasal side. In the tectum, the ligand eff-rin A rises from front to back.
scenes.visual: Growth cone with small sensing circle, then two opposite gradient bars

scenes.tts: Temporal axons carry the most Eff A, so a little eff-rin A repels them. Their endings form in the front of the tectum. Nasal axons carry little Eff A and tolerate more ephrin, so their endings form farther back. In chick and mouse, axons first overshoot, then branch, and eff-rin A blocks branches behind the right zone.
scenes.visual: Temporal and nasal axons overshoot their ending zones, then form branches; ephrin-A blocks branches behind each zone

Nasal axons carry little EphA and tolerate more ephrin, so their endings form farther back. In chick and mouse, axons first overshoot, then branch, and ephrin-A blocks branches behind the right zone.

scenes.tts: An axon might read an absolute level of Eff A, or compare itself with its neighbors. In mouse, researchers gave a scattered half of the retinal ganglion cells extra Eff A. If axons read absolute levels, only those cells should shift forward. Instead, with two copies of the knock-in, the cells with extra Eff A took the front of the target, and their normal neighbors were pushed to the back. Two orderly maps filled the target together.
scenes.visual: Normal map, half the cells marked purple, absolute prediction cleared, then purple take front and blue pushed back

scenes.tts: So each axon is judged against the others. Its ending depends on its Eff A signal relative to its neighbors. Axons compete for space, and the map is the outcome. Each growth cone senses only a short distance. Yet local rules give global order, partly because axons also sense each other.
